ground_truth.description: SessionSig.hashCallWithReplayProtection omits wallet address in hash, allowing signatures for one wallet to replay on another with same config and nonce. SessionManager.recoverSapientSignature and BaseAuth.signatureValidation do not bind to msg.sender.
ground_truth.root_cause: SessionSig.hashCallWithReplayProtection omits wallet address in hash, allowing signatures for one wallet to replay on another with same config and nonce. SessionManager.recoverSapientSignature and BaseAuth.signatureValidation do not bind to msg.sender.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Sign payload for Wallet A, replay on Wallet B (same config, nonce). Drains both wallets. PoC: test/extensions/sessions/SessionReplay.t.sol, run forge test --match-test test_crossWalletSessionReplayDrainsSiblingWallet -vv. Logs show attacker draining two wallets.
ground_truth.fix_description: Include address(this) in hashCallWithReplayProtection. Update SDK to hash (wallet, chainId, space, nonce, callIdx, call details).

vulnerabilities.explanation: The sessionPermissions memory array is pre-allocated using maxPermissionsSize = encoded.length / MIN_ENCODED_PERMISSION_SIZE (94). Each Permission node can be as small as 93 bytes. When permissionsCount exceeds the allocated length, direct indexing sig.sessionPermissions[permissionsCount++] writes past the array bounds, corrupting adjacent memory.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Submit a session configuration containing a single minimal FLAG_PERMISSIONS node (93 bytes). maxPermissionsSize becomes 0. The write to index 0 overwrites unrelated stack/memory variables (e.g. hasBlacklist, pointer, or return data), allowing the attacker to bypass identity signer, blacklist, or imageHash checks and produce a valid DecodedSignature for unauthorized calls.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Use a dynamically sized array with proper push (or pre-allocate with a safe upper bound such as encoded.length / 93 + 1) and avoid assembly length truncation until after all writes.

prediction.overall_explanation: The library performs unsafe manual memory allocation for a variable-length array whose size is underestimated relative to the minimum node encoding, enabling memory corruption that can be leveraged to forge valid session signatures.
